transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-21
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Leila Morrison (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Lyra Ops - Head of ML), Omar Reyes (Lyra Ops - Platform), Priya Kapoor (Lyra Ops - Finance), Tom Ward (Lyra Ops - SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Walkthrough of Redwood Console focusing on usage analytics and per-route cost. Discussed how to attribute cost to features and teams, options for Dedicated capacity, caching and batching impact, and compliance docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off — this should be mostly a console walkthrough, show the usage analytics and then drill into per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Ethan will take the demo.
[00:18] Ethan: cool, thanks Aisha. maya, priya, tom — thanks for making time. real quick can you remind us of your current setup? are you on a hosted provider today or running models in-house?
[00:32] Maya: yeah sure. we're currently deploying a mix — embeddings and generative completions on an internal cluster, kind of homegrown runtime. latency's fine for many but cost and ops are getting heavy. we're evaluating Redwood for predictable inference costs and easier rollouts.
[00:48] Omar: and on infra side we care about VPC access, KMS integration, and being able to route certain sensitive routes to private infra.
[00:56] Ethan: perfect. that's exactly what we'll highlight. first up — console home, usage trends. so here you can see token consumption over time, broken down by model and route. this is helpful to see which features are driving spend.
[01:20] Ethan: note — the per-route cost attribution ties the token counts to your billing rates; you can map routes to teams or product lines.
[01:33] Maya: is that per-token cost including caching effects? like how does the console handle prefix or KV cache reductions?
[01:42] Leila: good question. the dashboard shows both raw tokens consumed and billable tokens after cache/batching adjustments. we also flag cache hit rates on the route view. sometimes the transcription will show K V cash which is, uh, sorry, KV cache.
[01:58] Tom: little transcription humor there. ok. for PII routes we need to ensure requests never leave our VPC — how do you display routes that are private-only?
[02:10] Ethan: you can tag routes as 'private only' and the routing policy will send to your private deployment. Console shows a per-route deployment column and you can filter to see only routes on private hosts.
[02:26] Aisha: jumping in — on costs, one common ask is to understand cost per feature. we often recommend creating a route per feature so the dashboard shows exact spend. otherwise you see aggregate and it's hard to allocate.
[02:40] Priya: yes finance wants per-feature chargebacks. can we export monthly CSVs for accounting?
[02:46] Leila: yep exports, and we have an API endpoint for route-level usage so you can pull into your chargeback system.
[02:55] Ethan: now i'm going to open the route dashboard for your 'assistant-chat' route — you'll see latency percentiles, token breakdown, cost per 1k tokens, and a small panel estimating what you'd save with batching and with 8-bit quantization.
[03:14] Ethan: important to call out, quantization savings vary by model; console shows model-specific recommendations based on your observed prompt lengths.
[03:26] Maya: can you show an example of the cost breakdown?
[03:29] Ethan: sure. so for the last 30 days this route consumed about 12M input tokens and 36M output tokens, billable tokens after cache = 40M. at current SKU that's about $X, and if you enabled 4x batching you'd lower per-token cost by roughly 18% on peak windows — these are estimates.
[03:52] Omar: where does the 18% come from? is that from your bench or from our traffic profile?
[03:58] Ethan: a mix — console uses your real traffic shape, and the Optimize engine simulates batching and prefix K V cache effects. the number is conservative.
[04:09] Maya: is the Optimize engine public-facing? we want to be careful about trusting black-box estimates.
[04:16] Leila: it's transparent — you can see assumptions, e.g., average seq length, batching window, latency SLO. you can tweak them and recompute the savings.
[04:27] Priya: on the billing side, do you support committed reserved capacity for predictable spend?
[04:33] Aisha: yes that's Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with commit pricing. you get lower unit costs and dedicated throughput.
[04:41] Priya: what's the term length and typical uplift?
[04:44] Aisha: usually monthly or annual; discounts scale with commit. we'll include the SKUs in the deck.
[04:50] Tom: we need to validate SOC 2 and also encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.
[04:56] Aisha: we have SOC 2 and can integrate with KMS/HSM; we'll share security docs — I'll put the SOC 2 audit and the KMS integration guide in the follow-up.
[05:08] Ethan: back to console — another useful view is per-route cost trends correlated with latency. sometimes enabling batching reduces cost but slightly increases p95; the console helps you pick the sweet spot.
[05:22] Maya: can you show the per-team rollup — like map routes to engineering teams?
[05:27] Leila: yep — route tagging supports team, product, cost center; the top-level dashboard shows rollups with drilldown.
[05:35] Ethan: i'm going to open the anomaly detection tab — here's a recent spike we flagged driven by an upstream job that started sending long prompts. the console flagged the change and recommended looking at throttling or caching that workload.
[05:52] Omar: nice. that would have saved us a surprise bill last quarter.
[05:55] Maya: any integrations with observability — datadog, new relic?
[06:00] Leila: we have traces and export hooks — you can push metrics to Datadog or open telemetry or use our tracing link to stitch into your existing dashboards.
[06:12] Ethan: quick pause for questions.
[06:16] Maya: on the private deployment side — what are the rollback and canary features?
[06:21] Aisha: rollouts support canary by percentage and automatic fallback rules to older model versions or to hosted if private capacity degrades.
[06:32] Tom: curious about KV cache durability — if we have a hot prefix cache, do you need to persist it across restarts?
[06:39] Ethan: typically KV cache is ephemeral per instance; for mission-critical you can use persistent cache layers or warm up sequences via our warmup APIs. sometimes the transcript mishears KV as K V cash again, so noting that.
[06:55] Priya: going back to numbers, can you show a side-by-side of hosted vs Dedicated cost for our 3 main routes?
[07:02] Ethan: yes — pulling that. okay here we have hosted estimate: $Y/month; Dedicated committed is $Z/month with lower per-token.
[07:18] Leila: remember those are estimates; a perf POC will give more accurate numbers for your workload.
[07:24] Maya: what does the perf POC look like?
[07:27] Ethan: we typically run a week's worth of traffic replay at scale or targeted benchmarks; we can simulate peak qps and seq lengths and provide latency and cost numbers.
[07:38] Omar: do you support on-prem for our air-gapped environments?
[07:41] Aisha: yes "Redwood Private" can be deployed in VPC or on-prem; we have a control plane option that respects your network boundaries.
[07:52] Priya: ok finance question — if we go Dedicated and we underutilize, is there credit for unused capacity?
[07:59] Aisha: terms are negotiable; often we offer burst credits or flexible commit smoothing depending on contract. we'll put options in the proposal.
[08:09] Ethan: jumping ahead, here's the exports button — you can download CSV or call the usage API.
[08:15] Maya: great. any sample dashboards you share for our execs?
[08:18] Leila: yes we have a templated deck that maps console graphs to exec slides — we'll share that.
[08:25] Ethan: quick callout on tagging hygiene: we recommend a route naming and tagging convention to make cost attribution simpler.
[08:33] Tom: ok last technical q — what's the fallback behavior if private nodes go unhealthy during peak?
[08:38] Ethan: auto-fallback to hosted or to older model variant depending on your routing policy; you can set hard limits if you prohibit any egress.
[08:48] Priya: thanks folks, this is helpful.
[08:51] Aisha: cool, recap of next steps: i'll send pricing and SKUs; ethan will scope perf POC; maya will share traffic; priya and tom we'll set security deep-dive. thanks everyone.

[47:12] Aisha: recap — next steps: i'll send pricing and SKUs; ethan will scope perf POC; maya will share traffic; priya and tom we'll set security deep-dive. thanks everyone.
[47:31] Maya: great thanks.
[47:35] Meeting ended.
